messages:
maria: Pushed OFED 5.8.0 to euc3 during the night window for the security patch. Now seeing ~30-40% NCCL allreduce bandwidth drop on several p3/p4 training nodes. Anyone else seeing this?

raj: Saw it on two training jobs this morning. GPU util looks normal but allreduce times are way up. cc @kevin

kevin: Any quick numbers or commands you ran? Can you paste ibv_devinfo / ethtool / nccl-tests output from one affected host?

maria: Quick grab from gpu-euc3-12: 
```
$ ibv_devinfo -v | egrep "hca_id|fw_rev"
hca_id: mlx5_0
firmware: 16.29.1040
$ uname -a
Linux gpu-euc3-12 6.2.10-rt #1 SMP ...
$ ./build/all_reduce_perf -b 8 -e 16384 -f 2 -g 8
AllReduceBandwidth baseline ~45.2 GB/s -> now ~28.3 GB/s
```

sophia: Are those nodes on the new kernel too? We rolled kernel 6.2+ in that batch on Friday.

raj: Yes: kernel 6.2.10 + OFED 5.8.0. Did a quick rollback of OFED on gpu-euc3-12 and bandwidth jumped back to ~46 GB/s. Looks like OFED combo is the main suspect.

infra-bot: deploy:rollback requested by raj for euc3/ofed-upgrade on gpu-euc3-12 (runbook: infra/rdma/rollback)

ops-jen: Please pause the rest of the OFED rollout to euc1/euc2. This is affecting Dedicated training SLAs for two customers; need comms if rollback isn't clean.

kevin: Next data to collect: dmesg for mlx5 errors, /sys/class/infiniband/mlx5_0/ports/* counters, ib_mad stats, and RDMA CQ/SRQ drop counters. Also try ib_send_bw to reproduce. Workaround ideas: toggle tx offloads or test different firmware.

maria: Repro command I'm using: 
```
# run on a pair of hosts
$ ib_send_bw -F -d mlx5_0 <peer_ip> -s 4096 -D 10
# baseline on canary before upgrade ~48 GB/s, after upgrade ~30 GB/s
```

raj: Observed increased CQ errors and SRQ timeouts post-upgrade. Packet counts don't show obvious drops at NIC level, but RDMA layer reports retries/timeouts.

sophia: Could be a tx pacing or MLX5 tx-queue regression with this firmware + kernel. We saw a similar symptom months ago with coalesce settings. Worth validating firmware matrix.

kevin: I'll open a vendor case with Mellanox support and attach logs/traces. Also will try test toggling csum/sg offloads as a quick experiment. If that works we can script a temporary NIC config change cluster-wide.

maria: Canary rollback finished on gpu-euc3-12, perf restored. I'll collect full artifacts (dmesg, ibstat, ibv_devinfo, ethtool -S, nccl-tests) and upload.

ops-jen: Creating incident page and notifying affected customers. If rollback doesn't fully restore some nodes, we'll need a patch window. Incident: https://redwood.internal/incidents/OFED-EUC3-1919234567

kevin: Also exploring NCCL-level mitigation: forcing NCCL to use TCP for collectives for affected model containers as short-term stopgap (we can route across host network). Not ideal for latency but reduces SLA impact.

maria: Uploading artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-debug/ofed-euc3/1919234567/ (dmesg.tar.gz, ibv-devinfo.txt, ethtool-S.txt, nccl-run-output.txt)

raj: Plan: pause rollout, gather full hardware/firmware/kernel matrix for nodes in the batch, vendor ticket, and schedule a controlled retry after vendor confirms compatibility.

sophia: Agree. Assign kevin+raj to vendor engagement and rollback validation, maria to artifact collection and canary verification, ops-jen to customer comms.

maria: Thanks — blocking further OFED upgrades until we have a clear compatibility matrix and vendor response. Will update thread with vendor ticket number. :pray:
